hypotheses.H1: Verdana italic / bold-italic cases whose tip output differs from merge move toward Java; each such case MATCHes at tip whenever its same-consumer upright control (plain, or the creole ctl) MATCHes at tip, and is not a lost match vs merge.
hypotheses.H2: Verdana italic / bold-italic cases whose tip output equals merge: the consumer does not measure the italic slot; their Java status equals merge's (no gain, no loss); any failure with a matching control is a consumer gap outside the packet.
hypotheses.H3: Arial (all faces), other families (Times, Courier New, Helvetica, SansSerif, Monospaced, Lucida Grande): tip == merge byte-identical (already true in the predictions), so no lost match or gain.
hypotheses.H4: StateNodeFont italic removal (C5): every stateFontStyle form in Times / SansSerif gives tip == merge (true in predictions); Verdana sx cases change only through the italic tables.
hypotheses.H5: Queue pill (C3): Times queue cases tip == merge; Verdana queue cases change only in italic text widths, not in pill height.
hypotheses.H6: Sizes 9 and 23: per-glyph units x size reproduce Java widths for Verdana italic/bold-italic exactly where the plain control matches.
hypotheses.H7: Non-ASCII (na): T14.55 residue, no claim beyond 'no lost match vs merge'.
